materials.title: 一般过去时、did 与原因结果

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past sentence.
questions.evidence: Maya visited the center.
questions.explanation: 规则动词 visit 在这个过去事件中加 -ed。

questions.prompt: Choose the past form of write.
questions.evidence: She wrote an application.
questions.explanation: write 的不规则过去式是 wrote。

questions.prompt: Choose the past form of go.
questions.evidence: They went to the interview.
questions.explanation: go 的过去式为 went。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.evidence: She did not arrive late.
questions.explanation: did not 后用动词原形 arrive。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past question.
options: Does Maya met the manager yesterday?
questions.evidence: Did Maya meet the manager?
questions.explanation: Did 提前，主语后用 meet 原形。

questions.prompt: Choose the short affirmative answer to “Did Maya meet the manager?”
questions.evidence: Yes, she did.
questions.explanation: Did 问句的简短肯定回答使用 did。

questions.prompt: Complete: “She did not ___ late.”
questions.evidence: She did not arrive late.
questions.explanation: did not 后不再使用过去式 arrived。

questions.prompt: Complete: “Did Maya ___ the manager?”
questions.evidence: Did Maya meet the manager?
questions.explanation: Did 后的实义动词使用原形 meet。

questions.prompt: What does because introduce in the example?
options: An opposite result with no cause.
questions.evidence: Maya practiced because the interview was important.
questions.explanation: because 后 the interview was important 是练习的原因。

questions.prompt: What does so introduce in the example?
options: The reason the room was quiet.
questions.evidence: The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly.
questions.explanation: so 后 she spoke clearly 是前面安静环境对应的结果。

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that gives a reason.
options: Maya practiced because the interview was important.
Maya practiced because did the interview important.
Maya practiced so because the interview was important.
Maya practiced because so the interview was important.
answers: Maya practiced because the interview was important.
questions.evidence: Maya practiced because the interview was important.
questions.explanation: because 引出她练习的原因。

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that gives a result.
options: The room was quiet, so she speaked clearly.
The room was quiet, so did she spoke clearly.
The room was quiet, because so she spoke clearly.
The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly.
answers: The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly.
questions.evidence: The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly.
questions.explanation: 前句说明安静，so 引出她清楚说话这一结果。

materials.instructions: 阅读中文讲解及例句，再独立完成十二题并根据证据订正。
materials.passage:
1. 描述已结束的过去事件用一般过去时。规则动词通常加 -ed：Maya visited the center. 不规则形式需记忆：She wrote an application. They went to the interview. 时间线索如 yesterday 或 last week 有助判断，但动词也必须变为正确过去式；不说 she writed。

2. 过去时否定用 did not + 动词原形：She did not arrive late. 一般疑问句用 Did + 主语 + 动词原形：Did Maya meet the manager? 简短回答 Yes, she did. did 已承担过去时，不再把后面的动词写成过去式；不说 Did Maya met 或 did not arrived。

3. because 引出原因，so 引出结果：Maya practiced because the interview was important. The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly. 两个句子先找原因再找结果；一个基本句中不要重复使用 because ... so。because 和 so 所连接内容必须符合句意，不能只按位置猜测。

materials.title: Maya Prepares for a New Opportunity

questions.prompt: What position did Maya see?
options: A part-time assistant at a library.
A full-time assistant at the community center.
questions.evidence: On Monday, Maya saw a vacancy for a part-time visitor-desk position at a community center.
questions.explanation: 招聘的是社区中心的兼职访客服务台岗位。

questions.prompt: What experience did Maya and Lina share?
options: They organized a community education course.
They helped visitors at the community center.
They worked on separate library projects.
They worked together at a library reading event.
answers: They worked together at a library reading event.
questions.evidence: At the library, they had worked as a team during a busy reading event.
questions.explanation: 两人在图书馆阅读活动中曾共同工作。

questions.prompt: Which skill did Maya describe as her strongest?
options: Listening carefully to people who need help.
answers: Listening carefully to people who need help.
questions.evidence: Maya explained that her strongest skill was listening carefully when someone asked for help.
questions.explanation: 她强调在别人求助时认真倾听。

questions.prompt: What did the notice say about the computer course?
options: It was required for every candidate.
It was useful but not stated as required.
answers: It was useful but not stated as required.
questions.evidence: The notice mentioned the course as a useful qualification, but it did not say that the certificate was required.
questions.explanation: useful 不等于 required，文章没有说该证书为必需条件。

questions.prompt: What is Maya’s longer-term goal?
options: Take a full-time job with the local company.
questions.evidence: She wanted an opportunity to learn more, and her longer-term career goal was to work in community education.
questions.explanation: 她希望以后从事社区教育工作。

questions.prompt: What would Maya do if a visitor could not find a room?
options: Listen, check the list and ask a colleague if unsure.
Tell the visitor to wait while she checks a map.
Ask the manager to choose a room before speaking to the visitor.
answers: Listen, check the list and ask a colleague if unsure.
questions.evidence: Maya said she would listen, check the room list and ask a colleague when she was unsure.
questions.explanation: 她会先听、核对房间列表，不确定时询问同事。

questions.prompt: What is one responsibility of the visitor desk?
options: Prepare the center’s schedules for teachers.
Help visitors register for a course.
questions.evidence: During the conversation, the manager described the service and explained one responsibility: helping people find accurate information.
questions.explanation: 岗位责任之一是帮助访客找到准确信息。

questions.prompt: What hourly wage did the manager describe for the part-time role?
questions.evidence: The manager said the part-time role paid an hourly wage of twelve pounds.
questions.explanation: 兼职岗位时薪为十二英镑；月薪属于另一岗位。

questions.prompt: When would the center contact candidates?
questions.evidence: The manager said the center would contact candidates the following week.
questions.explanation: following week 表示下一周，不是面试当天。

questions.prompt: What does resume mean in the passage?
questions.evidence: Here resume means begin again; it is a verb, not the name of a job document.
questions.explanation: 这里 resume 是动词“重新开始”，不指求职简历。

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
materials.passage:
On Monday, Maya saw a vacancy for a part-time visitor-desk position at a community center. She wanted to learn about the role before sending an application. The notice said that the employee would help visitors find rooms and answer simple questions. Maya liked the idea because she had enjoyed helping people at a library.

Maya spoke to her former colleague, Lina, about her experience. At the library, they had worked as a team during a busy reading event. Maya explained that her strongest skill was listening carefully when someone asked for help. Lina remembered that Maya was reliable: she arrived on time and checked her work before leaving. This gave Maya a useful example to describe to the employer.

On Tuesday, Maya completed the application and listed a certificate from a basic computer course. The notice mentioned the course as a useful qualification, but it did not say that the certificate was required. Maya did not claim to have a qualification she had not earned. She wanted an opportunity to learn more, and her longer-term career goal was to work in community education.

The next morning, the center invited her to an interview with the manager of its visitor department. Maya brought the notice and a copy of her application. The manager asked each candidate to explain how they would respond if a customer could not find a room. Maya said she would listen, check the room list and ask a colleague when she was unsure. She also asked which task a new worker would learn first.

During the conversation, the manager described the service and explained one responsibility: helping people find accurate information. The visitor desk was run with support from a local company, whose main business was organizing community events. The manager said the part-time role paid an hourly wage of twelve pounds. A monthly salary appeared in a separate notice for a different, full-time role. Maya wrote down the difference and planned to ask about working hours before making any decision.

Maya did not receive a job offer at the interview. The manager said the center would contact candidates the following week. Maya felt successful in explaining her own example clearly, even though she did not yet know the result. On Thursday she planned to resume her library volunteering. Here resume means begin again; it is a verb, not the name of a job document. The profession interested her, so she kept the notes and thought about what she wanted to improve for the next conversation.

materials.title: A Different Interview Conversation

questions.prompt: When was Rina’s interview?
questions.evidence:
How was your interview at the neighborhood museum on Friday, Rina?
Rina: It was interesting. I went at eleven in the morning and spoke to the manager of the events department.
questions.explanation: Jo 先问星期五的面试，Rina 说上午十一点到达。

questions.prompt: What position did Rina apply for?
options: A visitor-desk employee at a clinic.
questions.evidence: The vacancy was for a weekend workshop assistant.
questions.explanation: 职位是周末工作坊助理。

questions.prompt: When did she send her application?
questions.evidence: I sent the application on Wednesday.
questions.explanation: Rina 说星期三提交申请。

questions.prompt: What certificate did she show?
options: A certificate from a first-aid course.
A certificate from a museum workshop.
A certificate from a short art course.
A certificate from a computer course.
answers: A certificate from a short art course.
questions.evidence: I showed a certificate from a short art course as one qualification.
questions.explanation: 她出示短期艺术课程证书，不是计算机课程证书。

questions.prompt: What example did she give of her experience?
options: Helping at a community sports event.
Working with a colleague at a library event.
Working with visitors at a museum workshop.
Working with a colleague at a garden event.
answers: Working with a colleague at a garden event.
questions.evidence: I described a garden event where my colleague and I worked as a team.
questions.explanation: Rina 用在花园活动与同事合作的经历举例；阅读中的 Maya 曾在图书馆工作。

questions.prompt: What was the hourly wage for Rina’s role?
questions.evidence: The hourly wage was fourteen pounds.
questions.explanation: 对话中的时薪是十四英镑；阅读另有十二英镑。

questions.prompt: What was the monthly salary associated with?
questions.evidence: The manager also mentioned a monthly salary, but that was for a different full-time position.
questions.explanation: but 后说明月薪属于另一全职职位。

questions.prompt: When will candidates be contacted?
questions.evidence: They will contact each candidate next Tuesday.
questions.explanation: next Tuesday 是通知候选人的时间。

questions.prompt: When will Rina resume her library volunteering?
questions.evidence: I will resume my library volunteering on Sunday.
questions.explanation: resume 在此为重新开始；时间是星期日。

questions.prompt: What does a new assistant do first?
options: Arrange the materials after the workshop ends.
Check the list of customers arriving late.
questions.evidence: A new assistant starts by preparing tables before visitors arrive.
questions.explanation: first responsibility 是访客到来前准备桌子。

materials.instructions: Listen to the two speakers and choose one answer. Use this dialogue rather than the reading passage.
materials.transcript:
Jo: How was your interview at the neighborhood museum on Friday, Rina?
Rina: It was interesting. I went at eleven in the morning and spoke to the manager of the events department.
Jo: What position did you apply for?
Rina: The vacancy was for a weekend workshop assistant. I sent the application on Wednesday. The employer wanted someone to help visitors find materials.
Jo: Did you give an example of your experience?
Rina: Yes. I described a garden event where my colleague and I worked as a team. I showed a certificate from a short art course as one qualification. I also brought a copy of my application for the manager.
Jo: What did they ask about?
Rina: They asked how I would help a customer who arrived late. I said I would listen, check the task list and ask an employee if I was unsure.
Jo: Did they explain the pay?
Rina: Yes. The hourly wage was fourteen pounds. The manager also mentioned a monthly salary, but that was for a different full-time position.
Jo: Did you get a decision at the interview?
Rina: No. They will contact each candidate next Tuesday. My goal was to speak clearly, and I felt successful in giving my example.
Jo: What will you do while you wait?
Rina: I will resume my library volunteering on Sunday. I enjoy that service, and I want to build a reliable work routine for my career.
Jo: Did you ask about the first responsibility?
Rina: Yes. A new assistant starts by preparing tables before visitors arrive. I wrote it in my notes, because this opportunity could teach me a new skill.

materials.title: Describe an Interview Experience
materials.instructions: Read the example aloud for practice, then record your own response with different details.
materials.prompt: Describe a fictional interview you attended. Say why you applied, describe one experience and skill you discussed, explain a question you asked, and say what happened afterwards. Speak for 90–120 seconds and use at least six different lesson words.
materials.reference: Last month I saw a vacancy at a community center and sent an application. I wanted the position because I enjoy helping people find useful information. At the interview, the manager asked about my experience. I described a library event where a colleague and I worked as a team. My example showed that I could listen to a customer and finish a task carefully. I also asked about the wage and the first responsibility in the department. The employer did not give me a decision that day, so I wrote down the date for a reply. After the interview, I planned to resume volunteering and practice another example for my career goal.

materials.title: An Application and Interview
materials.instructions: Write your own first draft using your own details. Do not copy the speaking example.
materials.prompt: Write 120–160 words about a fictional job application and interview. Explain why you applied, give one past experience and skill, describe a question about duties or pay, and explain what happened afterwards. Use at least six different lesson words, past simple, a did question or negative, and because or so.

guidedOutput.title: 写作结构提示
guidedOutput.text: Write four parts: the vacancy and application; your past example; the interview question and response; the result or next step. Use your own details. Here resume means “begin again,” not a job document.
